thread:
maia: Sharing a quick mock for the usage & billing page — want feedback on the vertical scope switch (Org / Project) vs the current horizontal tabs. Also prototyping denser invoice rows and a token-pill interaction for drilling into token breakdowns. Screenshot: https://faux.img/redwood/ux-vertical-scope.png jon: Nice! vertical switch could save horizontal real estate for charts. worried about discoverability though — will users notice it? :thinking_face: ravi: Agreed with jon. Maybe add a subtle label above: "View scope" or an inline tooltip on first hover. sarah: For invoice rows — dense layout is fine, but make sure each row retains a clear action affordance (download / dispute). Right now the mock hides actions behind a hover menu. hard for keyboard users. maia: Good call re: discoverability. Thinking a small chevron + label: "Scope: Org / Project". For keyboard nav we planned tabindex=0 on row and a visible focus ring. Thoughts? tay: Can we keep actions visible in condensed view as tiny icon buttons? that helps mouse + keyboard muscle memory. Also consider a secondary line for smaller invoices to avoid truncation. jon: +1 to visible icons. Also re: token-pill interaction — is that a popover or inline expand? mobile considerations? maia: Popover on desktop, full-screen drawer on mobile. Token-pill shows percent of total + clicking opens a mini table with per-model token counts and sample rows from invoice. Example pill: [Tokens 18.5k (45%)] — click -> popover. ravi: Love the pill idea. For accessibility, ensure the pill has aria-haspopup and aria-expanded attributes and the popover is focus-trapped. Sample snippet:```html
...
``` sarah: Also add aria-label that includes context, e.g. aria-label="Show token breakdown for invoice 2345, 18,500 tokens (45% of spend)" — helps screen reader users. maia: Nice. On the vertical switch: if we do vertical, it will sit left of charts and stay sticky when scrolling invoices. That gives more room horizontally for charts/time selector. But could push content on small screens. tay: What about a collapsible rail? default collapsed to an icon-only rail, expands on hover/focus. Keeps vertical affordance but saves space. jon: UX nit: the legend on the spend chart currently uses color + thin lines. Increase contrast & stroke width for accessibility. Also make legend items keyboard-focusable so you can toggle series with keyboard. maia: Good — update visual tokens to 3px stroke, add focus styles. Also debating invoice row density: condensed (6 rows per page) vs comfortable (4 rows). We could have a per-user preference in settings. ravi: Per-user preference seems safe. But default to comfortable for new users, condensed for power users. Add a toggle in the table header: "Row density: Comfortable / Condensed". sarah: Accessibility test: ensure condensed rows still have 44x44 tappable targets for action icons per WCAG touch target guidance. If icons are smaller, keep an invisible padding hit area. maia: Will do. One more question: org vs project scoping combined with date range — if someone changes scope, should date range persist? current mock resets range to last 30 days. tay: Persist date range. Changing scope shouldn't surprise users by altering filters unless they explicitly change it. jon: Agree. Also add a small toast on scope change: "Scope changed to Project: mobile-app — filters preserved." with an undo. design-bot: Auto-check results: contrast warnings on spend chart legend (AA fail), token-pill focus outline missing, table action icons < 44px interactive area. maia: Thanks everyone — I'll iterate and post updated frames. Quick TODOs: 1) make row actions icon-visible + keyboard focusable, 2) add aria labels for token pill/popover, 3) implement collapsible rail prototype for vertical scope, 4) increase legend contrast and stroke width, 5) persist date range on scope change. ravi: LGTM. Ping when ready for a quick review, will run accessibility checklist. :white_check_mark: sarah: If you want, I can run a 10-min keyboard nav pass after the next mock. maia: Awesome — appreciate it!
